set.body:
The README, both vignettes, and the package Description all open by describing the framework's construction rather than a question a researcher has. Quoted evidence:

  README.md:3-13   opens 'effectagram solves a task-fMRI problem' - good - but the sentence
                   runs 44 words and by its third clause is at 'turns partitioned experimental
                   effects into effect-space or measurement-space forms'. The next sentence:
                   'When the same named effects appear on both axes, an effect form specializes
                   to symmetric geometry.' A reader is asked to hold 'effect form', 'axes', and
                   'symmetric geometry' before learning what question gets answered.

  introduction.Rmd:15-19  'effectagram asks whether experimental effects reproduce across
                   declared partitions under a declared spatial measurement.' This is the best
                   single sentence in the docs and it is nearly right - 'do my effects replicate
                   across runs, and where' is a question every fMRI researcher has. But
                   'declared partitions' and 'declared spatial measurement' restate runs and
                   searchlights in framework vocabulary, so the sentence does not land.

  introduction.Rmd:29  first section heading is 'Declare the native relation'. The first thing
                   the reader is asked to do is a construction step, not a question.

  evidence-pairing.Rmd:21-26  'The hard part is not multiplying matrices; it is keeping the
                   experimental sample axis, neural measurement axes, covariance assumptions,
                   and normalization order honest.' This is the AUTHORS' hard part. It is a real
                   and defensible design thesis, but it is an answer to a question the reader
                   has not yet been given.

The pattern is consistent: the docs explain what the framework guarantees before establishing why a reader should want a guarantee. That ordering works for a reader who already believes the framework matters and inverts badly for one deciding whether to keep reading.

I want to be careful about what this bead does and does not claim. The vocabulary is not sloppy - it is unusually precise, and the precision is doing real work in the semantics the 0.1 chain established. The claim is narrower: precision that is load-bearing INTERNALLY has been placed at the point of FIRST CONTACT, where the reader has no way to know which distinctions are load-bearing and which are incidental.

Deliberately NOT proposing a rewrite yet. Four accessibility reviewers are mid-flight and one of them is a hands-on trial that will show empirically where a reader actually stalls. Proposing prose changes before that evidence lands would be guessing. This bead records the diagnosis and the quotes; remediation should wait for the trial.
set.title: Every user-facing entry point opens on machinery rather than a scientific question
